title: Per-build hook-point map
description: The artifact the hook-map generator emits every TMOS build (development-scope.md item 5; walkthrough build step 3): named symbol -> patchable entry + typed argument layout, signed and shipped with the image. A shield resolves its target hook by NAME against this map, and the signed binding is checked against it at load. REQUIRED here is scoped to what hook-point-map.json already carries, so that instance validates clean; the fields a real generator must add are marked '$comment: required in product'.

_comment.description: Free-text note. Present in the prototype instance.

tmos_version.description: Human-readable build version, e.g. '17.5.2'. Consumed by tmmtrace list.

build_id.description: Unique build identity. The signed binding's build_min..max range is expressed in these terms.

ctx_abi_version.description: Bumped whenever any hook's arg_btf changes shape. A function-boundary probe's ctx contract is build-specific; this is what makes a stale program detectable rather than silently mis-typed.

signature.description: Detached signature over the canonical serialization of this map. TMM carries only the public key (walkthrough build step 3).

name.description: The hook's stable name — what a shield names as its target, and what the binding's `hook` field pins. Bounded by SHIELD_HOOK_NAME_MAX (64) minus the NUL.

symbol.description: The build's symbol for this hook. Kept distinct from `name` so a catalog name can outlive a symbol rename.

attach_mode.description: observe = return value is telemetry only; filter = return value selects an enumerated outcome. Consumed by tmmtrace (it refuses drop() unless filter).

path_class.description: Cost class of the site: hot = per-packet/per-flow steady state, warm = per-connection/request, cold = exceptional/error/malformed branch. The budget pass gates against the ceiling implied here.
path_class.$comment: 'unclassified' is what phase A emits: cost classification needs call-graph and traffic analysis (phase B/C). Admitting a hook at 'unclassified' into ENFORCE is a decision to make deliberately, not a default --- the class exists to say how much a per-invocation cost matters on that path.

enumerated_outcomes.description: The host-owned actions available AT THIS SITE. A program may only choose among these; it cannot invent control flow.

arg_btf.description: The typed argument layout = the program's ctx. Emitted from the build's DWARF/BTF; also the input the PREVAIL program-type descriptor is generated from (item 6).
arg_btf.$comment: required in product; phase A cannot emit it (needs DWARF parameter classification)

abort_branch.description: Prose: how the host reaches its safe outcome here and what state, if any, must unwind. Present in the prototype instance.

entry_offset.description: Offset of the patchable entry pad from the symbol's address. Arm/disarm patches exactly here (item 2).

patchable_pad_bytes.description: Bytes of no-op reserved at the entry by -fpatchable-function-entry. Arm overwrites this pad; disarm restores it.

safe_return.$comment: required in product when attach_mode is filter
safe_return.description: What a skipped body hands back (item 7), gated on skippability FIRST. A hook is enforce-capable only when skippable is yes AND kind is not none — never on the return type alone.

budget_cycles.description: Per-invocation cycle ceiling for a program at this hook. The admission budget pass compares its longest-path estimate against this and fails closed (item 8).

mode_ceiling.description: The highest mode a program at this hook may ever reach. Enforcing sites sit behind a stricter authorization tier than observe-only.

entry.$comment: function entry address; the binary is non-PIE so this is also the runtime address

arm_at.$comment: where the 5-byte patch is written: entry+pad_offset for 'pad', entry for 'displace'

pad_offset.$comment: 4 = pad follows endbr64 (indirect-call targets); 0 = pad at entry (direct-call-only statics and .isra/.constprop clones). Absent when arm_method is 'displace'.

arm_method.$comment: 'pad' overwrites the compiler's nops and displaces NOTHING. 'displace' has no pad: the runtime copies displace_bytes of leading instructions to the trampoline verbatim, then writes the jump over them. Only emitted when those bytes are position-independent, so the runtime never decodes an instruction.

relocatable.$comment: leading instructions are position-independent, decided OFFLINE by mk_hook_map.py. Must be true wherever arm_method is 'displace'.

displace_bytes.$comment: total length of the WHOLE leading instructions covering >=5 bytes. Usually more than 5, because instructions cannot be split.

type.description: The C declaration of this argument, e.g. 'const struct ls_ctx *'.

ctx_size.description: sizeof the argument struct. This is the ONLY bound the verifier enforces — PREVAIL checks that an access lies in [0, size), not that it lands on a declared field. So ctx_size decides what a program can reach; the field list is documentation on top of it.

field_offsets.description: Authoritative byte offsets, emitted from the build's debug info (DW_AT_data_member_location) — NEVER re-derived by packing the field list. Re-packing is unsound: one omitted or untypeable field shifts every later offset, silently. Verified by check-offsets against the real header.

fields.description: Field name -> scalar type. No pointers out: every field is a fixed-width scalar or a small fixed byte array, so a predicate over it is PREVAIL's easy case.

skippable.description: GATE 1, and the one that decides enforce-capability. Does not running the body leave TMM consistent? Considers locks held across it, refcount movement, flow-state advance, input consumed, out-params the caller reads, and allocation. Default and absent-value semantics are 'unanalysed', which means observe-only: a body nobody has analysed is not safe-returnable, and 'we could not find a problem' is not 'there is none'. Mirrors enum shield_skippable in shield_abi.h.

kind.description: GATE 2, reached only after skippable is yes. none = gate 2 not reached; void = no value to synthesize, which says NOTHING about gate 1 (a void function is called entirely for its side effects, so void is the HARDEST case, not the trivial one); zero = 0/NULL is the benign no-op; const = return the enumerated benign value below. Mirrors enum shield_sr_kind in shield_abi.h.

value.description: kind=const only: the benign value the trampoline returns for a skipped body.

rationale.description: Why skipping this body is safe — specifically, the gate-1 evidence: which locks, refcounts, state advances, consumed buffers, out-params and allocations were checked and found absent. Also what benign work is lost while enforcing. A per-function human judgement, not a generated field, and required in product whenever skippable is yes.

key_id.description: Which F5 signing key; the public half is baked into TMM.
